analysis.title: Symbotic Inc. (SYM): Solid results and guidance; execution on growth opportunities in focus; 4QFY26 wrap
key_insights: GS reported 4QFY26 (Sept) revenue of $778 mn (+26% yoy, +8% qoq) and adjusted EBITDA of $114 mn, vs Street (FactSet) $774 mn / $104 mn. Revenue was near the top of the $760-780 mn guidance range.
1QFY27 guidance midpoint is revenue $815 mn and adjusted EBITDA $115 mn, vs Street $822 mn / $109 mn. Revenue guide is 0.9% below Street at midpoint and EBITDA is 5.5% above.
GS rates SYM Sell and cuts its 12-month price target to $33 from $42 to better reflect peer multiples. Price is $34.97, implying 5.6% downside.

Core business developments are mostly positive. The expanded Walmart agreement adds nearly $7 bn to backlog in 1QFY27 (up from $6 bn originally) and covers 25 US regional distribution centers plus international greenfield projects.

APD/SymMicro at Walmart: first prototype expected live in January and the second about 6 months later. Success would trigger orders for 400 stores (>$5 bn backlog), with an option for 200 more. Management thinks a third prototype is not needed and expects backlog recognition within 12 months.

Exol (formerly GreenBox) JV backlog of about $11 bn carries risk of restructuring or extension. Management said the full deployment timeline could be extended from the initial estimate. Multiple customers have been signed in grocery, e-commerce fulfillment and industrial, starting at the Atlanta site.

Total backlog fell slightly to $22.3 bn from $22.5 bn. About 16% (~$3.6 bn) is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months, similar to FY27 consensus revenue, with services and APD not included and thus incremental.

FY27 revenue is guided to be about 45%/55% 1H/2H weighted with sequential growth. Adjusted gross margin is stable in 1H and should improve in 2H as next-gen storage structure installs accelerate, with continued adjusted EBITDA margin expansion.

The sales funnel is at least twice as large as a year ago. Annual new customer additions could rise from 1-2 historically to 3-5 or more, and management expects a couple of large retail customers within 12 months. The company is exploring acquisitions and recently bought cellumation (sortation, European presence).

4QFY26 adjusted gross margin was 24.8% vs 25.0% in 3QFY26 and 22.1% in 4QFY25. FCF was about $353 mn in the quarter, with about $38 mn used for strategic investments. Non-GAAP EPS ex-SBC was $0.17, with a non-GAAP EPS bridge provided for the first time.
GS raises FY27/28 EPS (including SBC) to $0.51/$0.70 from $0.35/$0.55 and introduces FY29 at $0.85. FY27/28 revenue estimates rise to $3,752.8 mn/$4,259.3 mn from $3,588.0 mn/$4,127.0 mn.
Valuation is seen as expensive with high customer concentration. Stock trades at 68.4x FY27E P/E and 51.1x EV/EBITDA, and is down 34.8% over 12 months.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $33 from $42 on lower peer multiples (35x FY29 EBITDA vs 50x prior). Exol backlog risk, customer concentration and expensive valuation support the Sell.

earnings_insights: 4QFY26 (reported, Sept quarter): revenue $778 mn vs GS $778 mn and Street (FactSet) est $774 mn. Non-GAAP EBITDA ex-SBC $114 mn vs GS est $105 mn, Street est $104 mn and guidance $100-105 mn.
4QFY26 reported non-GAAP EPS ex-SBC $0.17. Non-GAAP EBITDA including SBC was $75.2 mn vs GS est $52.4 mn.
1QFY27 guidance: revenue $805-825 mn vs GS prior $837 mn and Street est $822 mn. Adjusted EBITDA $110-120 mn vs GS prior $117 mn and Street est $109 mn.
GS FY27E/28E/29E EPS including SBC: $0.51/$0.70/$0.85 (GS estimates). Excluding SBC: $0.85/$1.05/$1.20. FY27E/28E EBITDA ex-SBC $575 mn/$697 mn, FY29E $799 mn.
Systems started 10 in the quarter and completed 3. 1Q system starts expected roughly in line with 4Q.
risk_factors: Exol JV backlog (~$11 bn) could be restructured or extended given delays bringing on customers.
High customer concentration, with Walmart central to backlog.
Upside risks to the Sell: faster customer wins, faster system installation, accelerating warehouse automation investment, and better margins or fixed-cost leverage.
